newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica coffee sector urges production caution.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica coffee sector urges production caution.

text.p: Costa Rica coffee growers should exercise caution in the face of the recent sharp spike in prices and not take hasty decisions that could be damaging in the long run, officials said Friday.

"There are people who think that because prices have risen we can hike output and even stop sticking to export limits, but that can be counterproductive," Guillermo Canet, the executive director of the Costa Rican Coffee Institute, said.
Costa Rica and other members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) have set export limits per quarter that is a bid to control coffee flows and push up prices.
Basilio Rodriguez, secretary of the National Association of Small Farmers, said although the spike in prices is a relief for coffee farmers they should exercise caution about plans.

"Small coffee producers should remember that the market goes up and down on speculation and technical factors and people who want to distort the market, which is only usually a temporary factor," he said.
